the_bakery_line.title: The Bakery Line
the_bakery_line.story: You know how I found one of my best ideas? I was driving to the office in Pittsburgh and noticed the same thing every morning - a line out the door at this little regional coffee-and-bakery chain. Not just one location, but every one I passed. I thought, 'What kind of business has people lining up at 6am every single day, in February, in Pittsburgh?' Did my homework on the numbers, and it became one of my best investments. The lesson? Pay attention to what you see every day.
the_bakery_line.lesson: The best investments are hiding in plain sight in your daily routine.

joans_discovery.title: Joan's Discovery
joans_discovery.story: My wife Joan found this one. She kept coming home from the outlet mall with the same brand of kids' clothes - cheap, tough, and our boys could not wear them out, and believe me, they tried. She said, 'Every mother in that store is buying these.' I researched the company, and it was a home run. That's why I always say - some of the best stock tips come from your family, not Wall Street.
joans_discovery.lesson: Listen to the people around you. They often spot trends before analysts do.

the_diner_parking_lots.title: The Diner Parking Lots
the_diner_parking_lots.story: Driving my boys to away games all over western Pennsylvania, we'd stop at this regional diner chain. Every single one had a full parking lot - Tuesday night, Sunday morning, didn't matter. I thought, 'This company is crushing it, but nobody on Wall Street is talking about it.' Did my research - great numbers per location, loyal regulars, room to open in three more states. Sometimes the best opportunities are right in front of you, between the pancakes and the coffee refills.
the_diner_parking_lots.lesson: When you see a business thriving in the real world but ignored by Wall Street, dig deeper.

the_steel_town_turnaround.title: Buying When Everyone Was Scared
the_steel_town_turnaround.story: There was an industrial-parts maker outside Pittsburgh that everyone had written off. Layoffs, bad headlines, the whole thing. But I drove out to the plant, talked to the floor managers, looked at the new contracts they'd signed. The new management had a real plan. The stock was trading like it was going to zero, but I could see the turnaround coming. Bought it, and it was one of my biggest winners. The lesson? Do your own homework when everyone else is panicking.
the_steel_town_turnaround.lesson: Fear creates opportunity - but only if you've done the research to know what you're buying.

the_ten_bagger_miss.title: The One That Got Away
the_ten_bagger_miss.story: I missed a regional grocery chain that was reinventing how people shopped - bigger stores, better produce, prices that made everybody else nervous. Joan shopped there twice a week. I walked right by it. It went on to be a huge ten-bagger. Could've been in my portfolio but wasn't. That's the game, though. You can't catch them all. The key is to keep looking and not beat yourself up over the ones that got away.
the_ten_bagger_miss.lesson: Even the best investors miss great opportunities. Don't let regret stop you from finding the next one.
